title: Cold Spring Rising
premise: Coral Oyelaran takes a live-in nursing post at Hollowmere House, a private hospice where the dying all whisper the same countdown in their final hours. As mirrors begin lagging a second behind reality and the house's founding family closes ranks around a dying patriarch's inheritance papers, Coral realizes the count is not a symptom but a summons: the house collects its residents before they can sign away what it wants kept. Refusing to believe even as belief becomes survival, she smuggles the last resident, elderly Ada Voss, toward the gates ahead of the final number, discovering that her own invisibility was the house's oldest trick. The story ends with Coral burning the papers as the count reaches zero, trading her name to the house so Ada can walk free, and leaving Hollowmere reflected one second behind everyone else.
about_author: Wren Coldharbour spent six years as a night-shift caregiver before turning to fiction, and their horror is shaped by the hush of wards at 3 a.m. They write from a farmhouse in upstate New York where, they insist, every mirror is checked twice.

chapters.title: The Late Room
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral arrives at Hollowmere House for a trial week, noting its too-many mirrors and its owner's insistence that residents 'settle in permanently.' A dying man murmurs 'nine' at dusk. The beat is wary professionalism masking loneliness; Coral, used to being unseen, tells herself the whisper is morphine.

chapters.title: Nine
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The resident who said nine dies at dawn, and two others begin counting down within hours. Coral documents everything clinically, refusing pattern-seeking. The family matriarch, Verity Ashcombe, watches her too closely. Emotional beat: Coral's armor of skepticism cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: House Rules
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Verity hands Coral a laminated list of rules—no mirrors after dark, no visitors, no discussing the count. Coral breaks rule three immediately with fellow nurse Dev, who has worked here eleven years and gone quiet-eyed. Beat: unease curdling into institutional dread.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral catches her own reflection moving a beat late—a raised hand arriving after the hand. She smashes nothing; she measures it instead, timing the lag with her watch like a good nurse. Beat: terror converted into procedure, which fools no one, least of all herself.

chapters.title: Ada Voss Counts Too
chapters.summary: POV Coral. New favorite resident Ada, sharp-tongued and lucid, admits she hears the countdown and has known about it since 1974. She asks Coral, casually, to help her die somewhere else. Beat: the first open alliance, offered like a joke.

chapters.title: The Papers
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral discovers the estate documents every resident signs—deeds transferring not land but 'residence, perpetual.' Ada refuses to sign; the family lawyer arrives with velvet pressure. Beat: the horror acquires a legal face, and Coral's justice instinct ignites.

chapters.title: Dev's Eleven Years
chapters.summary: POV Dev. Dev reveals he once tried to walk a resident out; the man returned by morning with no memory and one fewer year of life. Dev begs Coral to stop seeing patterns. Beat: guilt and complicity—the cost of staying invisible too long.

chapters.title: What the Mirrors Keep
chapters.summary: POV Coral. At 3 a.m. the lagged reflections show rooms as they were decades ago: residents signing, residents refusing, residents being carried back through the front door. Coral sees herself in none of the old images. Beat: she understands why she was hired—she doesn't reflect right.

chapters.title: Verity's Grief
chapters.summary: POV Verity. Verity Ashcombe tends the house like a shrine, feeding it photographs and names, believing the count keeps her dead daughter 'near.' Her love and her cruelty are the same act. Beat: antagonist humanized; duty weaponized as devotion.

chapters.title: Seven
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Only seven residents remain, and the count accelerates—two die in one night, both mid-sentence. Coral finds their charts altered in her own handwriting. Beat: gaslighting made literal; Coral doubts her own record of reality.

chapters.title: The Gate Test
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral walks Ada to the gate on a pretext; fifty yards out, Ada's breath shortens, the count loudens in both their ears, and Ada turns back 'on her own.' Beat: hope ambushed—the house's reach measured in steps.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral and Dev, sleepless in the kitchen, admit what they've been avoiding—not romance exactly, but the unbearable fact of caring about someone inside a place designed to keep them. Beat: tenderness as rebellion; belonging chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Verity Reads the Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Verity. Verity finds Coral's copied notes and confronts her—not with anger but with an offer: help finish the count and Verity will let Coral leave untouched, unremembered. Beat: temptation of erasure, aimed precisely at Coral's oldest wound.

chapters.title: Six, Five
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Residents fall fast now; the mirrors lag two seconds, then three, showing Coral things she hasn't done yet—including herself holding a lit match. Beat: dread of foreknowledge; the reflection becomes prophecy.

chapters.title: Dev Disappears
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Dev vanishes between shifts; his room is repainted by morning, his name absent from every roster. Only Coral remembers him, and only in the lagging mirrors does his face still appear. Beat: grief and fury fused into resolve.

chapters.title: The Founding Count
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada tells the origin: in 1899 the Ashcombes counted their household down to seal a bargain—perpetual occupancy for the house, paid in residents. Ada was meant to be the final signature in '74 and escaped by faking her death. Beat: myth delivered as testimony; stakes become historical.

chapters.title: Zero Hour Papers
chapters.summary: POV Coral. The lawyer returns with a final document: if the last resident signs before the count ends, the house 'renews' and everyone else goes free—except whoever's name is written in the margin. Verity has written Coral's. Beat: betrayal crystallized; the trap fully visible.

chapters.title: Getting Out Ahead of the Count
chapters.summary: POV Coral. Coral and Ada run the gauntlet of corridors while the house rearranges itself—doors opening into 1974, mirrors showing them already caught. Coral uses her lagging reflection as a decoy, letting the house chase the image. Beat: ingenuity against inevitability; the count at three.

chapters.title: Two, One
chapters.summary: POV Coral. At the gate the count reaches two; Ada collapses, and Verity stands between them and freedom, begging Coral to understand that the house is all she has left of her daughter. Beat: the antagonist's heart broken open at the worst moment.

chapters.title: The Last Signature
chapters.summary: POV Coral. One. Coral signs the margin herself—trading her name, her reflection, her place in memory—to void the renewal clause. The papers burn without flame in her hands. Beat: sacrifice as authorship; Coral chooses to matter by choosing to be given up.

chapters.title: After the Count
chapters.summary: POV Ada. Ada walks out free into cold spring light; behind her, Hollowmere stands silent, its mirrors empty, its count finished. She carries Coral's name like a debt she intends to spend loudly. Beat: survivor's grief braided with purpose.

chapters.title: Cold Spring Rising
chapters.summary: POV Coral, elsewhere. In a town with no Hollowmere on any map, Coral works nights and catches, once, her reflection arriving a half-second early—as if something is giving back what she paid. She smiles. Beat: ambiguous grace; belonging finally chosen, at a price still echoing.
